open_points.question: Which generated consumer modules directly read `OWNER_FORM_FIELDS`, and which consumer → `data_provider` imports must therefore be declared?
options: Only the owner-form renderer reads it
Only the owner-request reader reads it
Both the renderer and reader read it directly
One facade reads it and supplies both
open_points.default_guess: Both the owner-form renderer and owner-request reader import `OWNER_FORM_FIELDS` directly from `data_provider`.

witness.initial: An owner form field is represented by a row of OWNER_FORM_FIELDS.
events: The owner-form renderer emits the field.
The owner-request reader interprets the submitted text.
outcomes: Both modules read the table, so a release change affects rendering and reading together.
Only one module reads the table while the other uses separately encoded field rules, so a release change can alter only one side.
witness.observer: The owner, when a rendered field is omitted or interpreted differently after the table changes.

open_points.subject: Model M29 Source of truth
open_points.text:
The release: the data provider's `OWNER_FORM_FIELDS`. The generated code
reads the table, so the data provider's constant delivers it (SPEC_STANDARD
§15.3.1), as it delivers the seven tables of M22–M28; a `models` catalog of
the same table would not reach the code, and none is declared.
open_points.rule: note, которая не должна создавать ребро, не называет чужой экспорт целым словом
open_points.question: Rewrite the model note so it does not name the foreign export `OWNER_FORM_FIELDS` as a whole word, and declare each actual consumer's import from `data_provider` structurally in `module_internal`.
